To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
F-theory compactified on elliptic Calabi-Yau fourfolds without section is described by M-theory compactified in the absence of a section on Calabi-Yau manifolds.

the five-dimensional effective action of M-theory compactifications is obtained from a six-dimensional effective action by reducing along a circle, that this reduction is accompanied by a shift-gauged action for the Kaluza- Klein vector, and that the shift-gauged axions are identified with the massive U( 1) gauge fields of the five-dimensional effective description.

the five-dimensional effective action obtained from M-theory on the Calabi-Ya threefold is identical to a six-dimensional F-theory effective theory reduced on an additional S1, the massive U( 1 )s are geometrically induced, and the massless U ( 1 ) is identified with the multi-section of M-theory on Calabi-Yau.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physics of compactifications of F-theory without section.
the physics of Ftheory compactifications without a section.
the study of F-theory on elliptic fibrations without section.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the physics of the five-dimensional effective action is completely captured by the six-dimensional F-theory action.
the physics of Ftheory compactifications without section is described by an effective action with a massless U( 1 ) vector, a charged hypermultiplets and a Chern-Simons term for the massless vector.
the physics of F-compactifications without a section can be described in five dimensions by an effective action that contains a massless U( 1) and a massive U(1).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the absence of a section in F-theory is captured in M-theory by non-trivial NS-NS and/or R-R three-forms along the circle and that the corresponding axions shift-gauge the massive U( 1 ) vectors of the fivedimensional theory.
the absence of a section in the Calabi-Yaw threefold of the M-theory setup is dual to the presence of a circle in the F-theory setup.
the massless U (1) in M-theory is identified with a U (1) vector that is massive and geometrically charged in F-theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the physics of F- theory compactifications on genusone fibrations with and without section can be described by the same five-dimensional setup.
the physics of Ftheory compactifications without section is well-understood from a five-dimensional perspective.
the massless vector of the five-dimensional effective action corresponds to the multi-section vector of M-theory.
